correctness.rationale: For any family of indexed embeddings, the simultaneous matching event has probability either zero or q^{-|U|}; letter coarsening only turns zero terms positive. The product expansion for t^{Z} and ordered-tuple moment expansion prove monotonicity. Shared-coordinate rank differences are at most n-m, giving full-law equality for n<m+d. A constructed pair with one newly compatible central collision occupies m+d sites, proving strictness for all n>=m+d, t>1 and orders r>=2. Constant and injective extremizers follow. A disjoint overlap-gap enumeration proves both second-moment formulas. The packaged independent enumeration checker passed 310 host cases, 160 formula cases and 3192 coarsening threshold comparisons using exact rational arithmetic. Finite tests are only corroboration.

value.rationale: The result addresses a natural deletion-channel ambiguity statistic under pattern letter identifications. The difference between equality of full laws up to a sharp host-length boundary and strict separation afterward is not visible from the common mean; it identifies precisely when repeated-letter dependencies become statistically observable. The all-length extremal order and explicit lower/upper second-moment formulas give structural bounds for all pattern lengths and alphabet sizes, rather than arbitrary small-case recomputation. The theorem does not rely on an unproved downstream application.
